title: Open-square exchange from restriction of direct image
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
{\scriptstyle j'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square with $j,j'$
open immersions.
On the small pro-etale sites,
the extension-by-zero functors
and derived pullbacks
admit a canonical natural isomorphism

$$
b_g:Lg^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*.
$$

Its restriction to $U'$ is the identity, after the pullback
identifications. These isomorphisms respect identity squares and
pasting of Cartesian squares.
(Source for the etale version:
[Stacks, Tag 03S6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03S6),
Lemma 59.70.5, the underived statement $j'_!f'^{-1}=f^{-1}j_!$ on
sheaves; the derived form and the compatibilities are proved below.)

proof.text:
Work first with sheaves of modules over the constant finite commutative ring $A$. Write $g^*$ for the underived module pullback. The coefficient identification and exactness in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] identify this with inverse image, with its transported $A$-action. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the sites of $U$ and $U'$ are the localizations at those opens and $j^*,j'^*$ are restriction, with the restricted constant coefficient rings. For $Q$ on $Y'$ and $V\to U$ in $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the direct-image formula in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives
$$
(j^*g_*Q)(V)=Q(Y'\times_Y V),\qquad
(g_{U*}j'^*Q)(V)=Q(U'\times_U V\longrightarrow Y').
$$
The Cartesian hypothesis identifies the two objects over $Y'$. Pullback along this identification gives a natural isomorphism $\delta_g:j^*g_*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{U*}j'^*$. For a morphism $V_1\to V_2$ the two restriction maps are induced by the same morphism of fibre products, so this is a sheaf map, not just an objectwise bijection. It is $A$-linear: by the definition of the coefficient structure map in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], both structure maps send each constant $a\in A$ to the same constant section, and maps from the constant sheaf are determined by these sections. This is the section calculation behind Stacks Tag 04J0 and the adjunction proof of Tag 03S6, now on the pro-etale sites.

source.place: Proof, first two paragraphs: direct-image restriction; agent adaptation of Stacks 04J0 (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites) and 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change)

proof.text:
Use the module adjunction $g^*\dashv g_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the extension-by-zero adjunction [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. The composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives
$$
 L_1=g^*j_!\dashv R_1=j^*g_*,\qquad
 L_2=j'_!g_U^*\dashv R_2=g_{U*}j'^*.
$$
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with its right-adjoint isomorphism $\delta_g^{-1}:R_2\to R_1$. It gives a canonical natural isomorphism $b_g^0:L_1\to L_2$, uniquely characterized by the composite units $\eta_1,\eta_2$ through
$$
R_1(b_g^0(F))\eta_{1,F}=\delta_{g,L_2F}^{-1}\eta_{2,F}.
$$
More explicitly, precomposition with $b_g^0(F)$ is the inverse of the natural Hom bijection
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(g^*j_!F,Q)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,j^*g_*Q)
\xrightarrow{\delta_g}\operatorname{Hom}(F,g_{U*}j'^*Q)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j'_!g_U^*F,Q).
$$
Thus both the direction and the adjunction data of the comparison are fixed.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: taking left adjoints; Stacks 03S6 adjunction argument, before derivation

proof.text:
The open adjunction units $F\to j^*j_!F$ and $N\to j'^*j'_!N$ are isomorphisms by [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit]. There are also canonical identifications $j^*j_*M=M$ and $j'^*j'_*N=N$: evaluating at $V\to U$ or $V'\to U'$ reduces them to $U\times_Y V=V$ and $U'\times_{Y'}V'=V'$. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies $g_*j'_*=j_*g_{U*}$, since both evaluate $N$ on $U'\times_Y W$ for $W\to Y$. Taking left adjoints with [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] and the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] fixes the usual pullback identification $j'^*g^*\cong g_U^*j^*$.
To check the restriction of $b_g^0(F)$, put $Q=j'_*N$ in the Hom bijection of Step 2 and apply $j'^*\dashv j'_*$ on both ends. After the displayed identifications and the open units, both ends are $\operatorname{Hom}(g_U^*F,N)$. The middle identification is
$$
j^*g_*j'_*N=j^*j_*g_{U*}N=g_{U*}N,
$$
and $\delta_g$ here is the identity on $N(U'\times_U V)$. The Hom bijection is therefore the identity, using the same $g_U$-adjunction on both sides. By the uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection], the restricted map is the identity of $g_U^*F$.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: normalization on U′; explicit Hom calculation replacing the assertion about the mate

proof.text:
For a second base change $h:Y''\to Y'$ let $U''=Y''\times_{Y'}U'$ and $h_U:U''\to U'$. Direct-image composition and its inverse-image comparison are fixed by the section formulas and [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], with the composite units of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Under those identifications the section calculation of Step 1 gives
$$
\delta_{g h}=(g_{U*}\delta_h)\circ(\delta_g h_*):
j^*g_*h_*\longrightarrow g_{U*}h_{U*}j''^*.
$$
Indeed both arrows evaluate a section on the unique identification of $Y''\times_Y V$ with $U''\times_U V$. Expand the Hom bijection of Step 2 for these two squares: its middle arrows are precisely $\delta_g h_*$ followed by $g_{U*}\delta_h$; the adjacent adjunction bijections combine to the composite adjunction. Consequently it is the Hom bijection for the outer square. Precomposition with the two resulting left maps is the same, so uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] gives
$$
b_{g h}^0(F)=b_h^0(g_U^*F)\circ h^*b_g^0(F).
$$
For $g=\mathrm{id}$, the section comparison and the Hom bijection are identities after the identity-adjunction identifications, so $b_{\mathrm{id}}^0=\mathrm{id}$ by the same uniqueness. These calculations use the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations].

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: identity and horizontal pasting; expanded section and Hom-bijection calculation

proof.text:
For vertical pasting let $i:V\hookrightarrow U$ be an open immersion, $V'=Y'\times_YV$, $i':V'\hookrightarrow U'$, and $g_V:V'\to V$. For $T\to V$, both composites of restrictions and direct images evaluate a sheaf $Q$ on $Y'\times_YT$, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. All reassociations preserve the projections, so are the same by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus the section comparisons of Step 1 satisfy
$$
\delta_g^{ji}=(\delta_{g_U}^{i}j'^*)\circ(i^*\delta_g^j):i^*j^*g_*\longrightarrow g_{V*}i'^*j'^*.
$$
This is an equality of module sheaf maps: the restrictions and constant-coefficient actions are precisely those already checked in Step 1.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: vertical pasting of the section comparisons

proof.text: The open adjunctions [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] give $j_!i_!\dashv i^*j^*$ and $j'_!i'_!\dashv i'^*j'^*$. Localization [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the right adjoints with $(ji)^*$ and $(j'i')^*$. Define the composition isomorphisms $(ji)_!\cong j_!i_!$ and $(j'i')_!\cong j'_!i'_!$ by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], using the identity on these right adjoints. These are the unique isomorphisms preserving the composite units. Hence, under them, the outer square's comparison is computed with those composite adjunctions, with no extra choice of a composition comparison.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: specify the open-extension composition comparisons by adjunction uniqueness

proof.text:
Write $c(-)$ for conjugation of transformations between left adjoints [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The Hom characterization in Step 2 says $c(b_g^{0,j})=(\delta_g^j)^{-1}$ and $c(b_{g_U}^{0,i})=(\delta_{g_U}^i)^{-1}$. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with an identity square for the extra adjunction $i_!\dashv i^*$ or $j'_!\dashv j'^*$, gives respectively
$$
c(b_g^{0,j}i_!)=i^*(\delta_g^j)^{-1},\qquad
c(j'_!b_{g_U}^{0,i})=(\delta_{g_U}^i)^{-1}j'^*.
$$
Here the other adjunctions are the $g^*\dashv g_*$ and $g_U^*\dashv g_{U*}$ adjunctions of Step 2 and their $g_V$ analogue; all composites are those of Step 6. Conjugation reverses composition by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Therefore for $B=(j'_!b_{g_U}^{0,i})\circ(b_g^{0,j}i_!)$,
$$
c(B)=\bigl(i^*(\delta_g^j)^{-1}\bigr)\circ\bigl((\delta_{g_U}^i)^{-1}j'^*\bigr)=(\delta_g^{ji})^{-1}=c(b_g^{0,ji}),
$$
where the middle equality is Step 5 inverted. Bijectivity of conjugation gives
$$
b_g^{0,ji}(F)=j'_!b_{g_U}^{0,i}(F)\circ b_g^{0,j}(i_!F).
$$
The identifications in Step 6 preserve units, so clause 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] permits exactly those changes of adjunctions. This proves vertical pasting using the cited mate calculus.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: vertical pasting by the generic composite-adjunction mate law (Mathlib mateEquiv_hcomp)

proof.text: If the open arrows are identities, the section comparison $\delta_g$ is the identity after restriction identifications. The middle restriction adjunctions in Step 2 are identity adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; its Hom bijection is the $g$-adjunction followed by its inverse. Equivalently, the conjugate comparison is the identity, whose inverse conjugate is the identity by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Thus $b_g^{0,\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}_{g^*}$. Together with Step 4 this checks both identity-square normalizations.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: the identity-open-arrow normalization

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], $j_!$ and $j'_!$ are exact on pro-etale $A$-module sheaves. The four pullbacks are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Apply these functors termwise to an arbitrary, possibly unbounded cochain complex $K$ on $U$. Naturality of $b_g^0$ with respect to each differential gives a chain isomorphism with components $b_g^0(K^r)$; the inverse is termwise $(b_g^0(K^r))^{-1}$. The exact-functor factorization theorem [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] shows that all these termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce the corresponding functors on the unbounded derived categories. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the induced pullback is $Lg^*$ (respectively $Lg_U^*$); the induced extension functors are denoted $j_!,j'_!$ since they are exact. The natural-transformation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore descends the chain isomorphism to
$$
b_g:Lg^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*.
$$
The normalization and identity and pasting equations of Steps 3--8 hold in every degree. The same localization theorem respects composition and detects equality of natural transformations after precomposition with the localization functor. It consequently gives all those equations on the derived categories. This proves every clause without a boundedness, constructibility, or stalk-detection hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph and last two sentences: derive the exact sheaf comparison and all its equations termwise

blueprint_update.statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
{\scriptstyle j'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square with $j,j'$
open immersions.
On the small pro-etale sites,
the extension-by-zero functors
and derived pullbacks
admit a canonical natural isomorphism

$$
b_g:Lg^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*.
$$

Its restriction to $U'$ is the identity, after the pullback
identifications. These isomorphisms respect identity squares and
pasting of Cartesian squares.

proof.text:
Restriction along an open immersion is localization of the site:
an object $V\to U$ is also an object over $Y$.
For a sheaf $Q$ on $Y'$, the direct-image formula gives

$$
(j^*g_*Q)(V)=Q(V\times_Y Y')
=(g_{U*}j'^*Q)(V).
$$

The equality respects restrictions and coverings on the site of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus $j^*g_*=g_{U*}j'^*$,
with all comparison maps specified on sections.

The exact functor $j'^*$ preserves injectives and K-injectives:
its left adjoint $j'_!$ is exact by
[def-weil-extension-by-zero]. For K-injectives this follows
directly by applying the adjunction to Hom complexes against an
acyclic complex. Thus a K-injective resolution of $Q$ computes
both sides of

$$
j^*Rg_*Q\simeq Rg_{U*}j'^*Q,
$$

using [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Taking left adjoints,
with the exact inverse-image pullbacks of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], gives
$Lg^*j_!\simeq j'_!Lg_U^*$. This defines $b_g$.
On $U'$ the section equality is the identity, so its mate has the
stated normalization. The section equalities for two pasted squares
compose to the equality for the outer square. The uniqueness of
left adjoints with their adjunction data proves the pasting and
identity assertions. This proof uses no claim that ordinary
geometric stalks detect arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.
